reason: I might download the free version because it stays on my phone with no account, and the doctor PDF would actually help. But I'm not paying for an AI write-up of my own log until I know what model it uses and what happens to my data, and breathing exercises won't help me get pregnant.
objection: The privacy promises are just claims on a landing page. 'You see what is sent first' still means my symptoms go to some AI company, and I've seen period apps say 'never sold' before. I also don't see any sign the patterns are grounded in actual PCOS guidelines rather than wellness fluff.
would_change_my_mind: An independent security or privacy audit I can read, plus Pro features that cite the international PCOS guideline and help with TTC, like ovulation-range tracking I can bring to my reproductive endocrinologist.
